subject: Mathematics
text: Euclid Division Lemma: For positive integers a and b, there exist unique non-negative integers q and r such that a = bq + r where 0 <= r < b. To find HCF: divide a by b to get remainder r; if r=0 then b is HCF; otherwise find HCF(b,r). Example: HCF(135,225): 225=135x1+90; 135=90x1+45; 90=45x2+0. So HCF=45. Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic: every composite number can be expressed as a unique product of primes. HCF = product of smallest power of each common prime. LCM = product of greatest power of each prime. HCF x LCM = product of the two numbers (only valid for two numbers).

subject: Mathematics
text: Proving irrationality: assume sqrt(2) = p/q in lowest terms; then 2 = p^2/q^2; p^2 = 2q^2; p is even; p=2m; 4m^2=2q^2; q^2=2m^2; q is even. Both p and q even contradicts lowest terms assumption. So sqrt(2) is irrational. Decimal expansions: rational number p/q (lowest terms) has terminating decimal expansion if and only if q has no prime factors other than 2 and 5. Example: 7/8 terminates (0.875); 1/6 is non-terminating repeating (0.1666...). Non-terminating non-repeating decimals are irrational. sqrt(2) = 1.41421356... is irrational.

subject: Mathematics
text: Polynomial p(x) degree = highest power with non-zero coefficient. Types: Linear (degree 1, 1 zero), Quadratic (degree 2, at most 2 zeroes), Cubic (degree 3, at most 3 zeroes). Zeroes are x-coordinates where graph crosses x-axis. For quadratic ax^2+bx+c with zeroes alpha and beta: sum of zeroes = alpha+beta = -b/a; product of zeroes = alpha x beta = c/a. To form quadratic: x^2 - (sum)x + (product). Division algorithm: Dividend = Divisor x Quotient + Remainder.

subject: Mathematics
chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
text: Pair of linear equations: a1x+b1y+c1=0 and a2x+b2y+c2=0. Three cases: (1) Unique solution (lines intersect): a1/a2 not equal to b1/b2. (2) Infinitely many solutions (lines coincident): a1/a2 = b1/b2 = c1/c2. (3) No solution (lines parallel): a1/a2 = b1/b2 but not equal to c1/c2. Methods: Substitution (express one variable in terms of other, substitute). Elimination (multiply to make coefficients equal, add or subtract). Cross multiplication: x/(b1c2-b2c1) = y/(c1a2-c2a1) = 1/(a1b2-a2b1).

subject: Mathematics
text: Quadratic equation ax^2+bx+c=0 where a is not 0. Methods: (1) Factorisation: find p and q where p+q=b and pxq=ac; rewrite middle term. (2) Completing the square: add (b/2a)^2 to both sides. (3) Quadratic formula: x = (-b +/- sqrt(b^2-4ac)) / 2a. Discriminant D = b^2-4ac: D>0 means two distinct real roots; D=0 means two equal roots (x = -b/2a); D<0 means no real roots. Sum of roots = -b/a. Product of roots = c/a. To form equation from roots: x^2 - (sum)x + (product) = 0.

subject: Mathematics
text: Arithmetic Progression (AP): sequence where consecutive terms have constant difference d. General form: a, a+d, a+2d, ... where a = first term. nth term: a_n = a + (n-1)d. Sum of first n terms: S_n = n/2 x [2a + (n-1)d] = n/2 x (first term + last term). Derivation: write S forwards and backwards, add pairs. Useful results: nth term = S_n - S_(n-1). Sum of first n natural numbers = n(n+1)/2. Three terms in AP: a-d, a, a+d. Example: AP 2,5,8,11... has a=2, d=3. 10th term = 2+9x3 = 29. Sum of first 20 terms = 20/2 x [4+57] = 610.

subject: Mathematics
text: Similar triangles: same shape, corresponding angles equal, corresponding sides proportional. Criteria: AA (two angles equal), SSS (all three sides proportional), SAS (two sides proportional and included angle equal). Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales): line parallel to one side of triangle divides other two sides in same ratio. If triangle ABC has DE parallel to BC then AD/DB = AE/EC. Properties: ratio of corresponding sides = k (scale factor); ratio of perimeters = k; ratio of areas = k^2. Pythagoras Theorem: in right-angled triangle, hypotenuse^2 = sum of squares of other two sides. Pythagorean triplets: (3,4,5), (5,12,13), (8,15,17).

subject: Mathematics
text: Distance formula: between (x1,y1) and (x2,y2) = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2). Section formula: point P dividing AB in ratio m:n internally = ((mx2+nx1)/(m+n), (my2+ny1)/(m+n)). Midpoint: ((x1+x2)/2, (y1+y2)/2) which is section formula with m=n=1. Centroid of triangle: G = ((x1+x2+x3)/3, (y1+y2+y3)/3). Area of triangle with vertices A(x1,y1), B(x2,y2), C(x3,y3): Area = (1/2)|x1(y2-y3)+x2(y3-y1)+x3(y1-y2)|. If area = 0, the three points are collinear. Collinear test: AB+BC=AC using distance formula.

subject: Mathematics
text: For angle A in right-angled triangle (right angle at C): sin A = opposite/hypotenuse = BC/AC. cos A = adjacent/hypotenuse = AB/AC. tan A = opposite/adjacent = BC/AB. Reciprocals: cosec A = 1/sin A; sec A = 1/cos A; cot A = 1/tan A. Also: tan A = sin A/cos A. Standard values table: sin 0=0, sin 30=1/2, sin 45=1/sqrt2, sin 60=sqrt3/2, sin 90=1. cos values are sin in reverse order. tan: 0, 1/sqrt3, 1, sqrt3, undefined. Trigonometric identities: sin^2 A + cos^2 A = 1; 1+tan^2 A = sec^2 A; 1+cot^2 A = cosec^2 A. Complementary angles: sin(90-A)=cos A; cos(90-A)=sin A; tan(90-A)=cot A.

subject: Mathematics
text: Angle of elevation: angle from horizontal upward to object above eye level. Angle of depression: angle from horizontal downward to object below eye level. Angle of elevation from point A to B equals angle of depression from B to A (alternate interior angles). Key formula: tan(theta) = height/base distance. Problem-solving approach: draw clear diagram, label known and unknown quantities, identify right-angled triangles, apply trigonometric ratios, solve equations. Example: if shadow of 6m pole is 2sqrt3 m, angle of elevation of sun = tan-1(6/2sqrt3) = tan-1(sqrt3) = 60 degrees.

subject: Mathematics
text: Tangent to circle touches at exactly one point (point of tangency). From external point: exactly 2 tangents. From point on circle: 1 tangent. From inside: 0 tangents. Theorem 1: tangent at any point is perpendicular to the radius at that point (angle OTP = 90 degrees). Theorem 2: lengths of two tangents from an external point are equal (PA = PB if P is external point, A and B are points of tangency). In quadrilateral OAPB: angle OAP = angle OBP = 90; so angle AOB + angle APB = 180 degrees. Application: finding unknown lengths in circle diagrams; circles inscribed in triangles.

subject: Mathematics
text: Arc length of sector with angle theta (degrees) = (theta/360) x 2 pi r. Area of sector = (theta/360) x pi r^2. Area of segment = area of sector - area of triangle. For triangle part: area = (1/2) x r^2 x sin(theta). Area of ring (annulus) = pi(R^2 - r^2). Key formulas: Circle area = pi r^2; Circumference = 2 pi r; Semicircle area = pi r^2 / 2. Combined figures: find areas of component shapes. Common values: pi = 22/7 or 3.14 as given. When asked to find shaded region: total area minus unshaded area. Equilateral triangle inscribed in circle of radius r has side = r sqrt 3.

subject: Mathematics
text: Cube (side a): SA = 6a^2; Volume = a^3. Cuboid (l,b,h): SA = 2(lb+bh+hl); Volume = lbh. Cylinder (r,h): CSA = 2 pi r h; Total SA = 2 pi r(r+h); Volume = pi r^2 h. Cone (r,l,h): CSA = pi r l; Total SA = pi r(r+l); Volume = (1/3) pi r^2 h; slant height l = sqrt(r^2+h^2). Sphere (r): SA = 4 pi r^2; Volume = (4/3) pi r^3. Hemisphere (r): CSA = 2 pi r^2; Total SA = 3 pi r^2; Volume = (2/3) pi r^3. Combined solids: volume is sum of parts; surface area = sum of exposed curved surfaces only. Frustum of cone (r,R,h): l=sqrt(h^2+(R-r)^2); CSA=pi l(R+r); Volume=(1/3)pi h(R^2+r^2+Rr).

subject: Mathematics
text: Mean for grouped data. Direct method: Mean = sum(f_i x_i) / sum(f_i) where x_i is class midpoint. Assumed mean method: Mean = a + sum(f_i x d_i)/sum(f_i) where d_i = x_i - a (assumed mean). Step deviation: Mean = a + h x sum(f_i x u_i)/sum(f_i) where u_i = d_i/h (h = class size). Mode for grouped data: Mode = l + [(f1-f0)/(2f1-f0-f2)] x h where l = lower boundary of modal class, f1 = frequency of modal class, f0 = frequency before, f2 = frequency after, h = class size. Median: find n/2 from cumulative frequency table. Median = l + [(n/2-cf)/f] x h. Empirical relation: Mode = 3 Median - 2 Mean.

subject: Mathematics
text: Probability P(E) = number of favourable outcomes / total number of equally likely outcomes. Range: 0 <= P(E) <= 1. P(not E) = 1 - P(E). Sample space = set of all possible outcomes. For fair coin: P(H) = P(T) = 1/2. For die: P(any number) = 1/6. Standard deck of 52 cards: 4 suits (Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, Spades), 13 cards each, 26 red cards, 26 black cards, 4 aces, 12 face cards (J,Q,K in each suit). P(ace) = 4/52 = 1/13. P(face card) = 12/52 = 3/13. P(heart) = 13/52 = 1/4. For two dice: total outcomes = 36. P(sum=7) = 6/36 = 1/6. P(doublet) = 6/36 = 1/6.
